title: C3265B — Front seat climate control module [SCME]
introduction:
This connector reference maps the front-seat climate control module’s temperature-sensor and control connections. I read it like a small switchboard for seat comfort: the important question is which seat and which function each connection belongs to.

Begin with the identification table, then match a cavity label in the drawing to its Cavity row. Read across for the circuit identifier, color, gauge, function and terminal information. Keep the driver/passenger and cushion/back wording attached to that row. Similar-looking temperature descriptions do not make the connections interchangeable, and the indicator and heater-switch assignments have different roles from the sensor connections.

This page supports identification and understanding of the assignments. It does not specify physical viewing direction, access, probing, test values or replacement steps. Gauge convention and the Size and Used codes remain undefined reference entries; use the matching service procedure before turning this map into electrical work.

edits.why: The drawing’s projecting housing structure is on the left, with a shaped outer edge on the right. I use those landmarks to stay oriented within the illustration. The shaded positions correspond to rows without assigned circuits or functions; their presence is not evidence of missing wiring. Page orientation alone does not establish a physical viewing direction.

Cavity links the drawing to the table, while Circuit Number identifies the electrical assignment. The Function column keeps the affected seat and sensing or control role explicit. Read those descriptions literally: related sensor and module labels do not establish signal direction, expected readings or a fault conclusion. Blank assignment fields provide no basis for inventing an additional function.

Number connects this record to Kit List above. Service Part and Engineering Shell distinguish the listed service item from its housing identifier, while Terminal Part Number remains with the individual cavity assignments. I use that distinction to keep the parts vocabulary straight; this table identifies a pigtail without teaching its installation.
